solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Food primarily with Greek character?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word food is used

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about some dish with a distinctly Greek personality.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the famous cheese of Greece is food with a Greek character.
explanation.definitionFit: This crumbly white cheese from sheep's milk is a staple of Greek cooking, so it is food with a Greek character.

clue.text: Support team to cheer on, having time for clubs

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means it replaces it, so time stands where clubs was

parts.note: to cheer someone on is to encourage them
C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: A backing group gets told to cheer someone on, with clubs swapped for time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having time for clubs' swaps the C of ENCOURAGE for a T.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants and helpers who travel with a celebrity and back them up.

clue.text: Sheepish when educated about meat not expected in burgers

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the first pair of pieces surrounds the meat

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
hamburgers famously contain no ham, so this is the meat you would not expect

explanation.surface: Someone feels sheepish once they learn their burger contains an unexpected meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamburgers take their name from the city of Hamburg, so the meat in the name is exactly what you do not find in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sheepish is feeling embarrassed or guilty about something you have done, a close synonym.

clue.text: Idly hum prose dreams of God? Quite the reverse

definitions.text: dreams of God? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: idly suggests aimless, random arrangement, so the letters of hum prose are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone lazily hums some prose and dreams of the divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the reverse' tells you to swap the definition round: not dreams of God but the god of dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the son of Hypnos is the deity who shapes dreams, giving his name to morphine.

clue.text: Possible description of aim as something rarely excellent

definitions.meaning: the word aim is the letter I (Roman one) sitting inside A and M (Roman thousand)
an exceptional person or thing, found only rarely

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic reading: in AIM, the I (one) is in A M (a thousand).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person or thing so exceptional that you would find only a single such case among a great many.

clue.text: Pat's one (male) — after sorting office's closure is averted

definitions.text: Pat's one (male) — after sorting office's closure is averted

indicators.note: sorting means putting into a new order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
averted means turned away, so the final letter of office is removed from the fodder

parts.note: the letters of these words are used as written

indicators.note: closure means the end, so the last letter of office is meant

explanation.surface: Postman Pat keeps his job when the local sorting office is saved from closing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PATSONE, drop the E at the end of 'office' ('closure ... is averted'), add M and rearrange ('sorting'). The whole clue also points to Postman Pat, the children's TV character.
explanation.definitionFit: Postman Pat is a British children's TV character, a mail carrier, so Pat's one is a letter carrier.

clue.text: Score-person's written up even slices for great golfer

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the letters run from bottom to top, so read backwards
even slices means the letters in even positions, the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A scorer's report praises a great golfer's even play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even slices' takes R, A, G, L, E from greAt GoLfEr; 'written up' turns them round. 'Score-person' is a composer, someone who writes musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations, so a writer of musical scores.

clue.text: Sergeant-major and confederate seizing father and unimportant people

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the father piece goes inside

parts.note: a confederate is an ally
FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A sergeant-major and his accomplice grab a priest and some nobodies.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for insignificant people comes from the term for young or small fish, too minor to bother with.

clue.text: Bond henchman James grapples with in another film

indicators.note: to grapple is to grip, so the James piece holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: JAS is the old written abbreviation of the name James

explanation.surface: A Bond villain's heavy wrestles with James in a different movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The steel-toothed villain from two Roger Moore films; 'in another film' also hints at Spielberg's shark movie of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The steel-toothed giant played by Richard Kiel serves the villains in The Spy Who Loved Me and Moonraker.

clue.text: Candid about half of guests, keeping elderly shut up

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the elderly piece is placed within

parts.note: candid means honest
elderly means old
on can mean about, as in 'a talk on birds'

indicators.note: half of means the first half of the letters of the word guests

explanation.surface: An outspoken guest silences an older person at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' sits at the far end of the clue but acts on 'Candid' and 'elderly'; 'about' gives a word of its own rather than signalling a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to keep quiet, a polite way of telling someone to stay silent.

clue.text: Temptation to tuck into muscle, a certain beef cut

indicators.note: to tuck into means going inside, so the temptation piece goes within the muscle piece

parts.note: AB is short for an abdominal muscle
an itch is a craving or temptation
a means one, a single thing

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted to tuck into a particular joint of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' does double duty in the surface but gives a word meaning one in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump bone of cattle gives its name to a cut of beef taken from around the buttock.

clue.text: American infantryman's returned letter

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American infantryman, and GI'S is the possessive

explanation.surface: A US soldier's letter comes back to him.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, the one used for summation in maths.

clue.text: With distraught mum aboard, glider possibly went into a dive

indicators.note: aboard means on a vehicle, so the jumbled mum letters ride inside the glider

parts.note: a sled glides over snow, so it is one kind of glider

indicators.note: distraught means badly upset, so the letters of mum are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A glider carrying an upset mother plunges into a nosedive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went into a dive' suggests a glider's plunge, but a dive is a seedy bar or club.
explanation.definitionFit: To slum it is to visit squalid places for fun, and a dive is a disreputable drinking den.

clue.text: Figure which formula remuneration packages overturned

indicators.note: overturned means flipped over, so the concealed letters read backwards
packages means wraps up inside, so the run of letters is concealed within these words

explanation.surface: A pay formula's packages get overturned on a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packages' gives LAREMUN within formuLA REMUNeration; 'overturned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral is a written symbol for a number, which is one sense of figure.

clue.text: Bond protagonist's musical talent behind piano augmenting note well

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the talent piece goes at the end

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
augmenting means adding to
NB stands for nota bene, Latin for note well
having an ear for music is having musical talent

explanation.surface: A musician's talent backs up a piano, adding a note well.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Bond wrote the children's books, so 'Bond' is the author, not 007.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmalade-loving bear from Peru is the hero of the children's books by the author Michael Bond.

clue.text: English mug welcoming one high point for leader

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the next pieces go inside the face

parts.note: mug and dial are both slang for the face
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tor is a rocky hill top, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An English face welcomes a high point for a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like a person, but in Britain it is also a newspaper's main opinion article. A tor is a rocky hilltop on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading article giving its own opinion is also called a leader in Britain.

clue.text: These layers of blame could make us scarce

indicators.note: could make says these letters can be formed into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Those who blame others could drive us into making ourselves scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: Layers here are people who lay something, so layers of blame are people who lay blame.
explanation.definitionFit: People who accuse others are laying blame on them, so they are, literally, layers of blame.

clue.text: Doctor Zhivago cackles making good old country now divided

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged
making good old means the good letter is made into the old one, a swap

explanation.surface: Doctor Zhivago laughs, leading to good things for an old divided country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making good old' turns the G of ZHIVAGO into O; 'Doctor' then shuffles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The central European state split peacefully in 1993 into the Czech Republic and Slovakia.

clue.text: Actor giving voice to 15 from army and navy

parts.note: a horde is a huge crowd or army
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: An actor voices a character drawn from the army and navy.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 15 is the Michael Bond bear, voiced by Michael Hordern in the 1970s TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Michael Hordern, an English character actor, narrated and voiced the bear in the 1975 BBC animation.

clue.text: Passionate part of right-winger's profession?

indicators.note: part of means only some of the declaration is used, dropping its opening word

parts.note: a conservative declaring loyalty would profess 'I am a Tory'

explanation.surface: Is a conservative's career a passionate one?
explanation.walkthrough: Profession here means declaration, not career. A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatory describes things relating to sexual love or desire, so passionate in that sense.

clue.text: After part exchange, fail to suffer

indicators.note: after the parts of the phrase change places, the two words swap order

parts.note: a business that fails goes under

explanation.surface: A car dealer's trade-in deal falls through, causing suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: Part exchange is a British term for trading in an old car against a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo hardship is to suffer or endure it.

clue.text: Something that impedes ring opponent for Rocky

parts.note: a drag is a hindrance or something that slows you down
O is a ring shape

explanation.surface: Something holding back a boxer's opponent in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivan Drago is the Soviet boxer Rocky fights in Rocky IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Drago is the Soviet boxer Rocky Balboa fights in Rocky IV.

clue.text: Casually leave waterfowl no longer served by kitchen

parts.note: a swan is a large waterfowl
a dish that is off is no longer available on the menu

explanation.surface: A water bird has been taken off the restaurant menu.
explanation.definitionFit: To go somewhere idly or in a carefree way, gliding away like the graceful bird.

clue.text: Vengeful deity bearing down heartlessly

indicators.note: heartlessly means without its middle, so the central letter is dropped

parts.note: an animal bearing down has fur or soft feathers on it

explanation.surface: A vengeful spirit bears down mercilessly on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' drops the middle R of FURRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Furies of Greek myth were goddesses of vengeance who pursued wrongdoers.

clue.text: Duck starter from Elizabeth David gets sent back

indicators.note: sent back means returned the other way, so the letters run backwards
the starter is the first letter of the word Elizabeth

parts.note: Dave is a short form of David

explanation.surface: A duck starter from cookery writer Elizabeth David is returned to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns E + DAVE round. Elizabeth David was a famous British cookery writer.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question is to dodge or avoid it, so the verb sense of duck.

clue.text: Deity more 'allowed when inserting new boat propeller

indicators.note: when inserting means putting the new letter inside the deity

parts.note: a deity is a god
'allowed is hallowed, holy, with the H dropped as in Cockney, so more holy loses its H too

explanation.surface: A god of more sacred standing propels a new boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'allowed shows a dropped H: hallowed means holy, and more holy minus its H gives OLIER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian boatman propels his gondola by standing at the stern with a single oar.

clue.text: Given too much information presented fraudulently, including name

indicators.note: including means containing, so the name letter goes inside

parts.note: spoofed means faked or passed off as genuine

explanation.surface: Someone who was fed false information that included a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts N inside SPOOFED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be spoon-fed is to be handed everything without having to think, as students with too much help.

clue.text: Express discomfort with work over engaging European

indicators.note: engaging means taking in or holding, so the European letter goes inside
over means turned over, so the work word is read backwards

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: A European worker complains about his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns PLY round; 'engaging' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp cry of pain is a way of expressing discomfort, especially from a dog.
